title: DevPlatform FinOps Analysis Report
subtitle: Cost Analysis and Optimization Recommendations

keyFindings: GitHub Actions consumed 812,500 minutes across 2 organizations
Total platform costs exceed $1,000/month - significant optimization opportunity

findings: Total Actions minutes: 812,500 across all workflows
Top consuming workflow: ci-pipeline in api-service repo (145,000 minutes/month)
15% of Actions minutes on macOS runners (10x cost multiplier)
Average Codespaces idle time: 18 hours/week per instance
concerns: acme-corp: 45.2% of Actions minutes on macOS (10x cost)
platform-team: Workflow integration-tests has 28% failure rate, wasting ~12,000 minutes/month

findings: Total licensed users: 37 (25 Basic, 12 Basic + Test Plans)
8 users inactive for >30 days (21.6% of total)

recommendations.title: Optimize macOS Runner Usage
recommendations.description: High macOS runner usage (45.2% of Actions minutes in acme-corp) at 10x the cost of Linux runners. Workflows are using macOS runners for tasks that could run on Linux.
implementationSteps: Audit all workflows using runs-on: macos-* runners
Identify workflows that don't require macOS-specific functionality
Move non-macOS tests to Linux runners (runs-on: ubuntu-latest)
Use conditional jobs: run macOS builds only for macOS-specific tests (UI, native features)
Consider using self-hosted macOS runners for frequently-run macOS jobs

recommendations.title: Remove Inactive Azure DevOps Licenses
recommendations.description: 8 users have not accessed Azure DevOps in >30 days but are consuming Basic licenses ($6/user/month) and Test Plans licenses ($52/user/month).
implementationSteps: Export user list with last access dates: az devops user list --org https://dev.azure.com/acme-devops
Contact users inactive >30 days to confirm if they still need access
Remove or downgrade licenses for confirmed inactive users
Set up monthly review process to identify and remove inactive licenses
Consider using Stakeholder licenses (free) for users who only need read access

recommendations.title: Fix High-Failure Workflows
recommendations.description: 7 workflows have failure rates >20%, wasting Actions minutes on failed runs that need to be re-run. Top offender: integration-tests in platform-team (28% failure, ~12,000 wasted minutes/month).
implementationSteps: Review workflow logs for integration-tests to identify root causes (flaky tests, race conditions, timeout issues)
Implement test retry logic for flaky tests: uses: nick-fields/retry@v2
Add better error handling and logging to diagnose failures faster
Split long-running integration tests into smaller, more focused jobs
Monitor failure rates weekly and address workflows >15% failure rate

recommendations.title: Optimize Codespaces Idle Time
recommendations.description: 5 Codespaces have been idle (no activity) for >7 days but remain running, consuming hours. Average idle time: 18 hours/week per instance.
implementationSteps: Set organization-wide idle timeout policy: Settings → Codespaces → Set idle timeout to 30 minutes
Enable Stop Codespace on disconnect feature in organization settings
Use prebuilds to reduce startup time, making it easier to stop/start Codespaces
Send reminders to developers with idle Codespaces >3 days
Consider scheduled cleanup script to stop Codespaces idle >7 days

recommendations.title: Rightsize Azure DevOps Parallel Jobs
recommendations.description: Analysis shows 2 hosted parallel jobs have <30% average utilization. You're paying for capacity that isn't being used. Current spend: $2,400/month on 12 jobs (8 hosted, 4 self-hosted).
implementationSteps: Review pipeline concurrency reports in Azure DevOps Analytics
Identify peak usage hours and typical concurrency needs
Reduce hosted parallel job count from 8 to 6 (-$80/month per job)
Optimize pipeline scheduling to spread load more evenly
Consider moving more workloads to self-hosted agents (ROI analysis shows 35% cost savings)

recommendations.title: Migrate to Self-Hosted Azure DevOps Agents
recommendations.description: Current mix: 8 hosted jobs ($40/month each = $320/month) + 4 self-hosted. ROI analysis shows migrating 4 more hosted jobs to self-hosted could save 35% on those workloads.
implementationSteps: Provision 4 additional self-hosted agent VMs (recommend Azure B2s instances: ~$30/month each)
Install and configure Azure Pipelines agents on new VMs
Create dedicated agent pools for self-hosted agents (e.g., self-hosted-linux, self-hosted-windows)
Migrate low-security pipelines to self-hosted agents first (test builds, linters)
Monitor performance and gradually migrate more pipelines
Expected savings: 4 hosted jobs ($160/month) - 4 VMs ($120/month) = $40/month, plus better performance

appendix.methodology: Analyzed platform usage data via GitHub and Azure DevOps APIs, calculated costs using current pricing rates, identified optimization opportunities.
appendix.pricingSource: GitHub Pricing (https://github.com/pricing) and Azure DevOps Pricing (https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/devops/azure-devops-services/)

_note: This is a sample report with realistic but fictional data for demonstration purposes. Actual costs will vary based on your organization's specific usage patterns.
